items.name: Nassau Hall
items.description: Princeton's oldest building, which served as the nation's capital in 1783.

items.name: Princeton University Chapel
items.description: Completed in 1928; the University opens and closes each academic year with a service here.

items.name: Princeton University Art Museum
items.description: The museum's bold new building opened to the public on October 31, 2025.

items.name: McCarter Theatre Center
items.description: Thornton Wilder's play Our Town had its premiere on McCarter's stage.

items.name: Palmer Square
items.description: Edgar Palmer announced this new town center for Princeton in February 1929.

items.name: Princeton Public Library
items.description: The Sands Library Building opened in 2004 and was hailed as a modern library.

items.name: Morven Museum & Garden
items.description: Built in the 1750s by Richard Stockton, a signer of the Declaration of Independence.

items.name: Princeton Battlefield
items.description: Site of the January 3, 1777 battle, called the fiercest fight of its size in the Revolution.

items.name: Princeton Battle Monument
items.description: Commissioned in 1908 and dedicated in 1922, with President Harding in attendance.

items.name: Drumthwacket
items.description: The official residence of New Jersey's governor, on land where the 1777 battle was fought.

items.name: Princeton Cemetery
items.description: Established in 1757 and still run by Nassau Presbyterian Church, near the center of town.

items.name: Updike Farmstead
items.description: A six-acre farmstead bought by the Historical Society of Princeton in 2004.

items.name: Lake Carnegie
items.description: A 3.5-mile lake made in 1906 when a dam at Kingston held back the Millstone River.

items.name: Institute Woods
items.description: 589 acres of woods, wetlands and farmland, gathered by the Institute for Advanced Study from 1936.

items.name: Marquand Park
items.description: Over 140 kinds of trees, including a Dawn Redwood once known only from fossils.

items.name: Herrontown Woods
items.description: Woods whose Veblen House was given to Mercer County in 1974 to become a nature museum.

items.name: Mountain Lakes Preserve
items.description: Friends of Princeton Open Space is planting over 6,500 native trees, shrubs and wildflowers here.

items.name: D&R Canal Towpath
items.description: The towpath of the Delaware and Raritan Canal, chartered by New Jersey in 1830.
